# Compute pack for Opus (generated by Rey, Oct 23, 2026)

Basis: repo main at 51337c2. Everything here was produced by mechanical extraction or by running the game's own sim harness at scale. The repo was read only; no game file was modified. The generator scripts are kept by Rey and can be rerun against any later HEAD to refresh the pack.

Purpose: answers Opus would otherwise re-derive by grepping or re-running sims at the start of a session, computed once and exhaustively. Treat counts and tables as data. Interpretations are marked as such and are Rey's external view, not code truth; code truth is Opus's.

## Files

### Content census (Run 3)
Extracted by loading data.js under Node the way sim3d.js does. Row counts: 45 hulls, 25 weapons, 36 boons, 12 relics, 13 modules, 24 admirals, 8 encounters, 6 factions.

- census_hulls.csv, census_weapons.csv, census_boons.csv, census_relics.csv, census_modules.csv, census_admirals.csv, census_encounters.csv, census_factions.csv: one row per content entry, id first, key fields in a stable order. Use for: any lookup of what exists, costs, stats, faction and patron membership, without re-parsing data.js. Note: boon d/fx fields are functions in source and appear in the CSV as function source text.
- content_census.md: row counts, per-faction and per-patron breakdowns, extraction notes.
- strings_corpus.csv: 1,507 player-facing string literals with file and line (data.js 798, ui3d.js 205). Use for: the IP vocabulary purge and any copy pass, as a single sweep list. The sweep is heuristic; a small residue of code-adjacent strings (selectors, filter names) is mixed in.

### Asset inventory (Run 4)
- asset_inventory.csv: all 553 asset files (157.5 MB) with type, size, and triangle counts for hull meshes. Triangle counts come from each mesh file's own stored t field, verified against the decoded index count divided by 3 for every mesh, zero mismatches.
- asset_inventory.md: totals and the SHIP_QUEUE reconciliation. Headline discrepancies, both computed: all 36 hulls have meshes plus material and normal maps in hulls/ and hulls_hi/ plus a concept painting, while 35 of 36 queue entries still read "not started" with no steps marked (only C19_51 has steps marked); and the pipeline README says the game loads CODE.vsm plus CODE_kit.json, while the repo contains zero .vsm and zero _kit.json files.

### Balance reference (Run 1, added when the run completes)
The game's own harness at scale: fuzz 2000, campaign 200 per cell (12 cells), bossmatrix 32, fmatrix 48, matrix 50 skirmish, archmatrix, plus the nine correctness checks as a header. Campaign used a scratch copy of sim3d.js with the known OBJS_SEEN guard patched in (the harness defect documented in contrib/muse/reviews/council/sim_matrix.md); the repo's sim3d.js was not modified. Files: balance_reference.md and per-mode CSVs.

### Code index (Run 2)
1,016 top-level definitions across the 18 build files (761 functions, 218 consts, 27 lets, 9 classes, 1 var). Zero names defined more than once.

- code_index.json: every definition with kind, file, line, total reference count across the build files plus head.html and sim3d.js, and the list of referencing files. code_index.md is the human summary (counts per file, the 30 most-referenced names, method and its limits).
- dead_code.md: 13 top-level names with zero references outside their own definition (CMD_HOLD, aiFocusTarget, faceToward, KIND_NAME, poolOK, muzzleFx, loftMesh, AIM_NAME, boltMat, vfxFadeDispose, volleyMuzzle, fxBookLoad, chargeFx). Each was confirmed definition-only by raw grep across the full corpus. The file carries the dynamic-dispatch caveats (string dispatch, ACT tables, window lookups, HTML handlers, Babylon RegisterClass) and per-name collision flags; do not delete on this evidence alone without checking those paths.
- referential_integrity.md: zero referenced-but-undefined ids across all 16 id categories (hulls, weapons, boons, relics, modules, admirals, commands, factions, patrons, encounters, abilities, perks, legacy, aspects, orders, weapon traits). 49 defined-but-never-referenced ids, concentrated in tables the game consumes by enumeration (16 of 24 admirals, 11 of 14 perks, all 12 legacy unlocks, 9 boons, 1 aspect); the report annotates each category with its enumeration sites, so those lists read as expected-by-design rather than deletion targets.
